title: Auditable export pipeline patterns and customer constraints
content:
Purpose:
This working doc collects recommended pipeline patterns for auditable SIEM exports (Splunk, Datadog, Azure Sentinel), customer onboarding constraints, and connector-level specs. Focus: make exports reproducible and evidence-friendly while minimizing customer configuration burden.

Status & audience:
- Status: in_review (security + platform + solutions engineering)
- Audience: security engineering, platform adapters, solutions engineering, customer SOC/infra teams

High-level goals:
1) Ensure every exported audit event is linkable back to a canonical Redwood audit record (event_id + model_version + route + request_id).
2) Preserve tamper-evidence where possible (HMAC or signature + KMS-backed key rotation notes).
3) Provide flexible per-customer mapping layers so customers can map Redwood fields -> their SIEM indexes with transform/PII redaction rules.
4) Define minimal RBAC v2 constraints so exports only include scopes the customer authorized.
5) Define runbook for evidence automation: how to collect, store, and prove export deliveries for compliance requests.

Design patterns (pipeline options):
A. Push-to-collector (recommended for quick onboarding)
   - Redwood acts as forwarder: batches events and POSTs them to customer HEC/HTTP collector (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs Intake, Sentinel EventHub/Log Analytics agent endpoint).
   - Use per-customer API key (scoped), TLS enforcement, and optional mutual TLS.
   - Advantages: minimal infra on customer side; Redwood controls retries and backpressure.
   - Drawbacks: customer needs to trust Redwood network egress and key custody.

B. Pull-from-queue (recommended for high-security customers)
   - Exported events land in a customer-owned queue (SQS/EventHub/GCP PubSub) or an S3 bucket; a customer-owned connector pulls, ingests into SIEM.
   - Advantages: customer retains custody, easier for air-gapped/private deployments.
   - Drawbacks: operational burden on customer; requires connector docs.

C. Hybrid relay (preferred for regulated customers)
   - Redwood writes to a customer-managed, short-lived pre-signed object store (S3), and signals customer via webhook/notification; customer pulls and ingests.
   - Adds audit of delivery (object written + notification).

RBAC v2 considerations (export scope model):
- Roles: export_viewer, export_admin, export_operator.
- Scopes: customer_id, project_id, dataset_tag (e.g., production/test), pii_allowed (true/false).
- Enforcement: connectors must validate the requesting service identity against RBAC token before sending any export.
- Entitlement checks: when enabling a SIEM connector for a customer, record the accepted scopes and attach to the connector config.
- Example policy: allow export_viewer to receive events with pii_allowed=false only; export_admin can enable pii_allowed=true after recorded justification.

Audit event schema (canonical Redwood audit format - minimal):
- event_id: string (UUID)
- timestamp: ISO8601
- customer_id: string
- project_id: string
- request_id: string
- route: string (API route or internal workflow)
- actor: { user_id | service_id } (string)
- action: string (generate, embed, model_load, config_change)
- outcome: string (success|failure|partial)
- model: string (model name + version)
- tokens: { input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int }
- cost_usd: number (optional)
- signatures: { hmac: string, key_id: string } (optional)
- redaction_flags: ["pii_masked", "partial_trace"]

Sample canonical event (stringified JSON for ingestion):
{
  "event_id": "4f3a1b2d-8f2d-4a42-9d6b-2c4e8a3b6a1e",
  "timestamp": "2025-05-12T17:21:03Z",
  "customer_id": "cust-842",
  "project_id": "proj-frontend",
  "request_id": "req-0011223344",
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "actor": "svc-ingest",
  "action": "generate",
  "outcome": "success",
  "model": "redwood-llama-13b:2025-04-01",
  "tokens": { "input_tokens": 34, "output_tokens": 120 },
  "cost_usd": 0.0045,
  "signatures": { "hmac": "<base64-hmac>", "key_id": "kms-2024-07" },
  "redaction_flags": ["pii_masked"]
}

Field mapping guidance (customer-facing mapping layer):
- Provide a small transform DSL in connector config: map('customer_index.user', 'actor') or redact('customer_index.text', 'email')
- Default mappings:
   - customer_index.timestamp <- timestamp
   - customer_index.source <- route
   - customer_index.event_id <- event_id
   - customer_index.severity <- map outcome to severity (failure -> high)
- Redaction rules must run before signing.

Delivery protocols & minimal connector specs:
1) Splunk HEC (recommended settings)
   - Endpoint: https://<customer-hec-host>:8088/services/collector/event
   - Auth: HEC token (store token id in connector config), optionally mTLS
   - Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
   - Batch: max 1000 events or 5MB per request
   - Retry: exponential backoff with jitter, max 5 retries; if failure persists, write to durable retry S3 and alert ops
   - Example curl (single event):
     curl -k -H 'Authorization: Splunk <HEC_TOKEN>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"event": <canonical_event_json>}' https://customer-hec:8088/services/collector/event

2) Datadog Logs Intake
   - Endpoint: https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input
   - Auth: API_KEY in header 'DD-API-KEY' or query param (prefer header)
   - Rate limits: respect Datadog account ingestion limits; implement local rate controller (tokens/sec) and exponential backoff
   - Example curl: curl -H 'DD-API-KEY: <API_KEY>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '<canonical_event_json>' https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input

3) Azure Sentinel (Log Analytics / Event Hub pattern)
   - Preferred: push to a customer-managed Event Hub with SAS credentials (preferred for dedicated/private)
   - Alternative: push to Log Analytics HTTP Data Collector API (requires workspace ID + shared key)
   - Example: for Event Hub, publish Avro/JSON to topic <customer-hub> using AMQP over TLS; include message property 'redwood-event-id'

Security controls around delivery:
- Key rotation: connectors must reference key_id rather than raw secrets; rotate and maintain historical key mapping for signature verification.
- Proof-of-delivery: maintain delivery receipts with: event_id, send_timestamp, http_status, response_body (truncated), retry_count. Keep receipts for 1 year by default (configurable per-customer).
- Tamper-evidence: HMAC-sign the canonical event body (before mapping/redaction) and include key_id in the envelope. Document verification steps for customers.

Evidence automation: what compliance asks often:
- Provide exported events for a date range linked to the canonical event IDs and delivery receipts.
- Provide a signed manifest for a collection (manifest includes list of event_ids, counts, hmac root hash, created_at).
- Automation tasks: manifest generation, signed-upload to customer S3, and an audit trail entry in Redwood's internal audit DB.

Customer onboarding checklist (minimum required fields from SOC/customer):
- Export mode: push | pull | hybrid
- Preferred collector: Splunk HEC / Datadog / EventHub / Other (URL)
- Auth mechanism: token | mTLS | SAS | workspace-key
- TLS requirement: TLS1.3 only? client cert required?
- Expected throughput (events/sec) and retention needs (days)
- PII policy: allow pii_allowed? examples of fields to exclude
- Compliance must-haves: evidence retention period, SOC2-specific artifacts, allowed jurisdictions for data egress
- Contact: SOC on-call escalation emails and Slack workspace handle

Operational runbook (alerts & troubleshooting):
- Alert triggers:
   - >10% of daily exports failing (5xx HTTP) -> create P1 incident
   - Persistent enqueue backlog > 10k events -> P2, throttle new exports and notify customer
   - Signature verification failure rate spike -> P1 (possible key mismatch)
- Quick checks:
   1) Confirm connector config (endpoint, token ID, key_id) in console
   2) Check delivery receipts for last successful send timestamp
   3) If HEC 400 errors: validate event JSON schema and required fields
   4) For Datadog 429: consult customer on ingestion limits, recommend rate limiting profile

Testing & validation matrix (acceptance criteria):
- Schema validation: 1000 synthetic events pass ingestion to staging HEC and are visible in their index with event_id present
- Proof-of-delivery: manifest generation for a 24-hour window matches receipts and counts
- RBAC enforcement: attempts to enable pii_allowed without export_admin role must fail (automated test)
- Failover: when primary collector unreachable, secondary mode uses durable staging (S3) and no data loss for 72 hours

Open questions / decisions to make (action items):
- Should Redwood sign events before or after applying customer mapping/redaction? (current recommendation: sign canonical raw event and include signature in envelope; customers can re-sign after their local mapping if they choose)
- Default retention for receipts: 1 year vs 2 years (legal ask pending from compliance team, see SEC-321)
- Level of transform DSL complexity: keep tiny (map, rename, redact, copy) vs allow arbitrary JS transforms (security risk)

Next steps (owners):
- Marisol: draft lightweight transform DSL spec (due 2025-01-10)
- Liam: implement HEC batching + retry logic in siem-adapters (PR GHA-879)
- Priya: finalize RBAC v2 scope docs and update connector onboarding UI (due 2025-02-15)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc intended for cross-team feedback. Please add comments inline or link to SEC-321 and GHA-879 when proposing changes.

Appendix A: customer-friendly sample mapping snippet (YAML-like pseudo config)
connector_config:
  mode: push
  protocol: splunk_hec
  endpoint: https://hec.example-corp.com:8088/services/collector/event
  auth: { token_id: token-77, key_id: kms-2024-07 }
  batch: { max_events: 500, max_bytes: 5242880 }
  transforms:
    - map: { to: "index.user", from: "actor" }
    - redact: { field: "index.text", type: "email" }

Appendix B: quick verification commands (staging)
- Splunk HEC: curl -H 'Authorization: Splunk <TOKEN>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"event": {"event_id": "test-1", "timestamp": "2025-05-12T00:00:00Z"}}' https://staging-hec.redwood.test:8088/services/collector/event
- Datadog: curl -H 'DD-API-KEY: <KEY>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"message": "test", "ddsource": "redwood-test", "event_id": "test-1"}' https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input

-- end of working doc --
